messages:
maria: Heads-up — we've been seeing sustained egress tail and latency wobble from tenant `mammoth-ml` in eu-west for the last 3 hours. Spikes correlate with long-running finetune jobs and lots of KV cache churn. Thinking we should try a 'soft segmentation' carveout to limit their egress and protect shared slices.
kevin: Can you paste the top-level metrics? egress bytes, p95 token latencies, and which pools they're hitting?
maria: Quick snapshot: egress ~120MB/min (steady for 2h), p95 token latency up from 140ms->310ms on shared-slice-7, KV cache miss rate jumped 18%. Pools: shared-slice-7, shared-slice-8, a few warm-pools in eu-west-1.
olivia: Oof. Are they on dedicated? I thought mammoth-ml had a fractional dedicated carve last month but maybe it fell back.
maria: They were on fractional reserved, but fallback happened at 08:12 UTC when a host drain evicted their warm slots. Requests spilled to shared slices.
rui: Suggestion: create a short-lived soft carve that reduces their egress ceiling and nudges allocator to place retry traffic into a low-cost preemptible pool. We can avoid hard preemption to keep latency acceptable.
kevin: Agree. We need two things: 1) immediate mitigation (soft egress cap + prefer preemptible warm-pool) 2) follow-up: detect and auto-quarantine heavy KV churning tenants for a rolling backoff.
maria: Proposed one-line mitigation run now:
```
# soft carve egress for tenant + prefer preemptible warm-pool routing
poolctl carve --tenant=mammoth-ml --egress-limit=6mbps --mode=soft --prefer-pool=preemptible-warm-eu-west
```
kevin: That CLI looks fine, run it with a 10m TTL so we can observe. Add a fallback policy to cut to 3mbps if p95 stays >250ms for 5m.
maria: Doing it now (running with 10m TTL + fallback).
deploy-bot: poolctl accepted: action_id=ac-99823, executed by maria at 2876543220.
maria: Initial telemetry after 90s: egress dropped to ~7MB/min, p95 dropped to 190ms, KV miss rate unchanged for now. Good first-order signal.
olivia: Nice. Can we make the allocator prefer fractional-dedicated backfills for this tenant next time? If fallback triggers often we should pin more consistent capacity.
rui: Agreed — propose a 'cohort shepherd' label that groups tenants by workload profile (finetune/batch vs interactive) and applies different routing + egress budgets. This avoids blanket policies that penalize interactive apps.
kevin: Love the cohort idea. Operationally: 1) label at tenant creation 2) routing policy engine picks cohort and applies a small set of levers (egress cap, KV cache priority, pool preference). Need to ensure billing/alerts align.
maria: Also callout: cost impact analysis — if we push more into preemptible pools we save ~22% cost but raise miss/retry rates slightly; fine for batch workloads but not for QC interactive customers.
olivia: I'll draft a short runbook for 'soft-segmentation' (mitigate -> observe -> escalate -> pin capacity) and add sample poolctl commands + rollback steps.
kevin: Add a metric alert: when a single tenant's egress >50MB/min sustained for 10m AND p95 >200ms on shared pool -> auto soft-carve with TTL 10m. That should catch most noisy neighbor cases early.
rui: And we should store a short history of soft-carves per tenant (sliding window) so we can recommend reserved capacity sales outreach after N carve events/week.
sre-bot: Alert created: noisy-tenant-auto-carve (thresholds: egress>50MB/min, p95>200ms, sustained 10m). Policy attached to eu-west clusters.
maria: Great. I'll follow up with the quick runbook and a PR to the allocator to add cohort labels. Leaving the temporary carve running until 2876543820 (10m TTL + buffer).
kevin: Thanks — please ping in 8m with final verdict. :thumbsup: 
olivia: +1 and add cost delta estimate to the PR.
rui: I'll prototype the cohort label mapping this afternoon and share.
maria: Thanks team, closing the thread for now unless the carve escalates. :lock:
